- **Position constraints:** I computed each part's transform from its hole centres, so the hole-to-hole matches (lower arm, upper arm, shade lug, bulb cap) should land within tolerance. The bracket foot sits on the base top edge.
- **Bracket upright:** the L bracket has two equal-length arms, so I chose which one is the upright by assuming the bracket is a standard unmirrored "L". Its pin hole is the one near the end of the arm I rotated to vertical.
- **Elbow plate:** its three holes form an equilateral triangle. I took the bottom hole and right hole to be the ones that make the plate sit roughly vertex-down.
- **Head plate:** I assumed its arm hole is the one hole of a different size, and hole A is the bottom one.
- **Shade and bulb:** I flipped the shade so its open end faces right and slightly down. The lug then sits on top, under the head plate. The bulb is rotated to point out of the open end.
- **Arm ends:** the two ends of each arm look identical, so which end goes to which joint is arbitrary; I picked one.
